tool.name: FusePlotsAndField

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/geometric-tools/fuse-plots-and-field.html
Combines a field (boundary) polygon layer and a research-plot polygon layer into one feature class in which every piece of ground carries exactly one treatment rate. The research plot polygons themselves are cut out of the original field polygon, so there are no overlapping features.
The research plot polygons carry their own treatment rate from their original feature class, and the surrounding field polygon either has a standard treatment rate applied or takes it from an existing field in the field feature class. If the treatment polygons were created with the Plot Designer tool, then the treatment rates for each plot were assigned at that time and are available in the Rate attribute field that the tool created.
Selections are honored on both layers. The output carries Rate, Source (Field or Plot), Plot_FID and Field_FID plus the plot layer's attributes. A port of the CropCentric Fuse Plot and Boundary Feature Class tool (Jenness and Wiebers 2018). Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
What it makes. A prescription map: one polygon feature class in which every piece of ground carries exactly one rate. Each field polygon (a map layer's selection honored) is kept as its own feature carrying its rate -- nothing is dissolved, so two field polygons with the same rate stay two features; then every plot is subtracted from the field polygons (geometry differences, no Advanced license needed), and the plots themselves are appended with their own rate. Field remainders that vanish entirely are dropped.
Rates. The plot rate comes from the plot rate field (a plot with an empty value gets the standard rate, or 0 if there is none, with a warning). Ground from the surrounding field is assigned rate values from the field rate field where it has a value, and the standard rate otherwise; give one of them or both.
Attributes. Rate (double), Source ('Field' or 'Plot'), Plot_FID (the plot's ObjectID; -1 for field ground) and Field_FID (the field polygon's ObjectID; -1 for a plot), then the plot layer's own attribute fields (blank on field ground) unless the copy is switched off; names are shortened for shapefiles.
Coordinate systems. The output uses the field layer's coordinate system (or the Output Coordinate System environment); plots in another system are projected into it with the datum transformation the environment chooses. Curved (true-arc) polygons are densified first.

dialogReference.para: The field or boundary polygons. A map layer's selection is honored.
The research plots, from the Plot Designer or any polygon layer. A selection is honored.
The numeric field of the plot layer holding each plot's rate (Rate for Plot Designer outputs).
The fused polygons: the field polygons with the plots cut out, plus the plots, each with its rate. A geodatabase feature class or a shapefile.
A numeric field of the field layer holding the rate of field ground. Where it is empty the standard rate is used.

param.name: standard_rate
param.displayname: Standard rate for field ground (used where no field rate field is given, or the field's rate is empty)

dialogReference.para: One rate for all field ground without a rate of its own. Required when no field rate field is given.

param.name: transfer_plot_fields
param.displayname: Copy the plot layer's attribute fields to the output

dialogReference.para: Checked (default): the plot layer's attribute fields are added to the output and filled for the plots (blank for field ground).

scriptExample.title: Fuse Plots and Field example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: The field's own rate attribute, with 120 as the standard rate for field polygons that lack one.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.FusePlotsAndField( field_layer=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Fields", plot_layer=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots_2026", plot_rate_field="Rate", out_fc=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Prescription_2026", field_rate_field="FieldRate", standard_rate=120, transfer_plot_fields=True)
